# Installing Writ Desktop

Download the installer for your platform from the
[latest release](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-desktop/releases/latest).

## macOS

Requires **macOS 11 Big Sur or newer**. There are two builds — take the `aarch64` one on
Apple silicon (M1 and later) and the `x64` one on an Intel Mac. If you pick the wrong
one it simply will not launch.

1. Open the `.dmg` and drag **Writ** to Applications.
2. Launch it from Applications.

The build is signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized by Apple, so Gatekeeper
should let it open normally. If you see "Writ can't be opened because Apple cannot check
it for malicious software", you almost certainly have a partial download — re-download
and check the hash (below) rather than working around Gatekeeper on a binary you can't
verify.

## Windows

Requires **Windows 10 or newer** (x64).

Run the `.msi` (or `.exe`) and follow the installer. The default install is per-machine
and needs administrator rights.

**This build is not yet Authenticode-signed.** SmartScreen will show *"Windows protected
your PC"* and name the publisher as unknown; choose **More info → Run anyway** to
continue. Because Windows cannot vouch for the file for you, verify it against
`SHA256SUMS` (below) before running it — on this platform that check is doing real work,
not ceremony.

## Linux

Requires **glibc 2.35 or newer** (Ubuntu 22.04 and equivalents) with a working
WebKitGTK. Builds are published for **x86_64** and **arm64** — match your machine
(`uname -m`).

```bash
# Debian / Ubuntu
sudo dpkg -i writ_*.deb && sudo apt-get -f install

# Anything else
chmod +x Writ_*.AppImage && ./Writ_*.AppImage
```

Linux packages are not OS-signed on any distribution; `SHA256SUMS` plus the signed
update manifest is the integrity story here.

## Verifying your download

Every release includes `SHA256SUMS`. Download it alongside the installer and:

```bash
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing     # macOS / Linux
```

```powershell
Get-FileHash .\Writ_x64_en-US.msi -Algorithm SHA256   # Windows — compare to SHA256SUMS
```

The hashes are computed from the **signed** artifacts, so they match exactly what you
downloaded.

## First launch

A short setup wizard runs once. It covers:

1. **Language** — English, French, or Spanish.
2. **Browser runtime.** Writ drives a real Chromium to record and replay. If you already
   have Chrome or Chromium installed, it is detected and used. Otherwise the app downloads
   a private copy of **open-source Chromium** (**about 150-330 MB**, depending on platform)
   into its own directory — it is used only by Writ and never touches the browser you use
   every day. This is the only download the app makes on first run.

   The download is pinned to a specific Chromium revision and checked against a SHA-256
   built into the application before it is ever launched; a binary that does not match is
   refused. Writ does not redistribute a browser — you obtain it from its publisher.
3. **Launch at login** — optional; keeps scheduled monitors and API calls working
   without the window open.
4. **Connect your AI** — optional one-click MCP setup for Claude Desktop, Claude Code,
   ChatGPT, or Codex.

You can re-run the wizard any time from **Settings → General → Re-run setup**.

### Installing without an internet connection

The app itself works offline; only the one-time browser download needs the network. If the
machine cannot reach the internet, either install Chromium/Chrome through your usual
channel (Writ detects it) or copy the runtime directory across from a machine that can. The
path is shown in **Settings → Engine & Data**.

On **arm64 Linux** there is no published open-source Chromium build to download, so install
it with your package manager (`sudo apt install chromium`) — Writ will detect it.

## Where things are installed

| | macOS | Windows | Linux |
|---|---|---|---|
| Application | `/Applications/Writ.app` | `C:\Program Files\Writ` | `/usr/bin/writ` (deb) |
| Your data | `~/.writ` | `%USERPROFILE%\.writ` | `~/.writ` |

Everything the app creates — your encrypted database, downloaded browser runtime, logs —
lives under the data directory. Deleting it resets the app to a fresh install.

## Uninstalling

Remove the application, then delete `~/.writ` if you also want your workflows and
credentials gone. Uninstalling the app alone leaves your data in place so a reinstall
picks up where you left off.

If you enabled "launch at login", turn it off in **Settings → General** *before*
uninstalling, or remove the login item manually afterwards.

Record a web task once. Replay it forever — on your own machine.

Turn any website into a workflow, a REST API, or an MCP tool your AI assistant can call.

Install · What it does · Connect your AI · Troubleshooting · Security · Report a bug

--- **Writ Desktop** records a repeatable browser task once and replays it forever — no re-scraping, no brittle scripts, no per-run AI cost. It is a desktop app: the engine runs on your machine as a loopback-only background process, your workflows and credentials stay in an encrypted database in your home directory, and nothing leaves the machine unless you explicitly link a cloud account. > **This repository is the download and issue tracker for the app.** Writ Desktop is > proprietary and its source is not published here — see [`LICENSE`](./LICENSE). Nothing in this README should be read as exceeding it. ## Open source Writ Desktop is proprietary, but it is built on projects that are not: | Project | What it is | |---|---| | [`usewrit/writ-agent`](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-agent) | the Rust engine the app drives — the same binary ships inside the app | | [`usewrit/writ`](https://github.com/usewrit/writ) | the self-hosted coordinator: `docker compose up` and run the whole thing on your own server | | [`usewrit/writ-sdks`](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-sdks) | Python, TypeScript, Rust, and Go clients | | [`writ-mcp`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/writ-mcp) | the MCP connector, on npm | Every open-source component bundled in the app is listed with its full licence text in [`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`](./THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md), which is regenerated from the dependency graph on every release and also readable inside the app under **Settings → About → Open-source licences**. ## Support - **Bug or crash** → [open an issue](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-desktop/issues/new/choose). # Security Policy — Writ Desktop

This is the **authoritative security-claims document** for the open-source Writ
desktop app (the single `writ-agent` / `writ-agentd` Rust process + Tauri shell).
Marketing copy, the README, and the in-app UI **must not exceed** the bounded
claims stated here. It implements **PRODUCTION_READINESS.md PROD-21** and is the
single source of truth referenced by **PROD-24** for the bounded-claims
reconciliation.

> **Scope of this file.** This covers the *local-first desktop application* —
> the `writ-agent` crate built on `--features local`
> as the `writ-agentd` daemon, plus the Tauri shell. The hosted **Writ Cloud**
> service has its own separate security documentation and its own disclosure
> intake. Org-level SOC 2 attaches to Writ Cloud, **not** to the single-user
> offline desktop.

---

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Please report security issues privately. Do not open a public GitHub issue for
a vulnerability.**

Use **either** channel:

1. **Email:** `security@usewrit.app` — PGP key available on request. Encrypt
   anything sensitive (proof-of-concept, exploit details).
2. **GitHub private advisory:** open a draft advisory via *Security → Report a
   vulnerability* on the `writ-desktop` repository. This keeps the report private
   until a coordinated fix ships.

Please include: affected version (see the supported-versions table below), OS +
architecture, reproduction steps or a proof-of-concept, and the impact you
believe it has. **Never include real credentials, secrets, or extracted data** in
a report — redact them.

### Response targets (coordinated disclosure)

We follow a coordinated-disclosure model. Indicative targets (best-effort for an
OSS project, not a contractual SLA):

| Stage | Target |
|---|---|
| Acknowledge receipt | within **3 business days** |
| Initial triage + severity assessment | within **10 business days** |
| Fix or mitigation plan communicated | within **30 days** for High/Critical |
| Public disclosure / advisory | **coordinated** with the reporter, typically after a fix ships or **90 days**, whichever comes first |

If we cannot meet a target we will say so and keep you updated. We will credit
reporters in the advisory and the CHANGELOG **Security** section unless you ask to
remain anonymous.

### Safe harbor

We will **not** pursue or support legal action against good-faith security
research that:

- respects the disclosure process above and gives us reasonable time to fix
  before public disclosure;
- targets **your own installation** of the app (the desktop app is local-first;
  do not attack other people's machines or the hosted Writ Cloud
  infrastructure of other tenants);
- does not exfiltrate data beyond the minimum needed to demonstrate the issue,
  does not degrade service for others, and does not violate privacy or applicable
  law.

Activity consistent with this policy is considered authorized. If in doubt about
whether an action is in scope, ask first at `security@usewrit.app`.

### Bounty

There is **no paid bug-bounty program at launch.** Intake is **coordinated
disclosure via private advisory / email with safe harbor** only. We credit
reporters publicly (with consent). A paid bounty may be introduced later; this
section is the authoritative statement until then.

---

## Supported versions

Security fixes are backported to the versions below. We are a fast-moving
single-binary OSS app, so the supported window is intentionally narrow:

| Version line | Supported | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Latest minor (e.g. `1.x` newest) | ✅ Yes | All security fixes land here first. |
| Previous minor | ✅ Yes (security only) | Critical/High fixes backported until the next minor ships. |
| Older minors | ❌ No | Upgrade to a supported line. |
| Pre-1.0 / beta builds | ❌ No | Dogfood/beta builds receive no backports. |

The app version is single-sourced from the `writ-agent` crate's `Cargo.toml`
(`writ-agent` crate, currently `1.0.0`). The bundled **Chromium** revision is
versioned on a **separate axis** and updated
independently; a Chromium security update may ship as a patch release without an
app feature change. Check `CHANGELOG.md` for the per-release Security section.

---

## What is protected — and what is NOT (bounded scope)

This section is the load-bearing honesty boundary. It mirrors
**SECURITY_AND_ENTITLEMENTS_SPEC.md §1.6** and **DESKTOP_APP_PLAN.md §0** exactly.
**No other document or marketing surface may claim more than this.**

### At-rest encryption — what it IS

All local data is encrypted at rest using three layers
(SECURITY_AND_ENTITLEMENTS_SPEC.md §1.1):

- **Layer A — whole database.** Everything in `writ.db` (and its `-wal`/`-shm`)
  — workflow steps, runs, extracted data, monitor content, automations, **all
  columns** — is encrypted with **SQLCipher (AES-256)**, transparent per-page.
- **Layer B — field AEAD.** Credential and secret blobs are additionally sealed
  with **XChaCha20-Poly1305** (magic `WF1`, random 192-bit nonce, AAD bound to
  `table|column|row_id`) on top of Layer A — defense in depth for the
  highest-value columns only.
- **Layer C — files.** `~/.writ/files`, `artifacts/` (workflow output,
  screenshots, diffs), and `logs/` are encrypted with **age STREAM**
  (ChaCha20-Poly1305, 64 KiB chunks; per-file key derived via HKDF).

The root key (random 32 bytes) lives in the **OS keyring**
(`writ-vault/master`); every layer key is HKDF-derived from it. In-memory key
material uses `secrecy` + `zeroize`.

**Threat model this defends against:** a **stolen or lost laptop**, **another
local user or process**, **malware reading files at rest**, and **leaked backups
or copied `~/.writ` directories**.

**Bounded compliance claim:** *"AES-256 / XChaCha20-Poly1305 encryption at rest,
satisfying SOC 2 CC6.1 / GDPR Art. 32 **intent**."* This is an intent/posture
claim, not an attestation.

### What is explicitly NOT claimed

We deliberately do **not** claim any of the following, and you should treat any
copy that does as a bug to be fixed:

- ❌ **Not FIPS-validated.** RustCrypto (`chacha20poly1305`, `argon2`, etc.) and
  `age` are not FIPS 140-validated cryptographic modules.
- ❌ **Not HSM-backed.** Keys live in the OS keyring / a `0600` file fallback,
  not a hardware security module.
- ❌ **No anti-swap pinned memory.** `zeroize` is best-effort; Rust/LLVM register
  spills and OS swap can retain plaintext copies. Memory is not pinned.
- ❌ **Not full-disk-encryption equivalent.** At-rest encryption protects the
  data files; it is not a substitute for OS full-disk encryption on a *running,
  unlocked* machine.
- ❌ **No zero-knowledge once linked.** When you opt into Writ Cloud, a metered
  cloud call necessarily transmits the call inputs, the chosen result, and
  duration/status metadata. We do not claim zero-knowledge after linking.
- ❌ **No protection on a running, unlocked machine** against a privileged local
  attacker. Once unlocked, the key is in memory by design.
- ❌ **Recipe/IP is not cryptographically protected.** Workflow recipes are
  protected only by access control and the metadata-only catalog projection
  (see CLOUD_LINK_CONTRACT.md), not by cryptography against a determined operator
  of their own machine.
- ❌ **gVisor / isolated-execution tier is not operational** in the desktop and
  is **not advertised** as an entitlement (`isolated_execution = "n/a"`).
- ❌ **True single-file crypto-erase is not guaranteed.** Under a shared
  file-master key, per-file crypto-erase is impossible without a wrapped-per-file
  key column; "Delete my data" is best-effort `secure_delete` + DB row removal.
  See the data-erasure stance below.

---

## The `vault.key` file-fallback disclosure (weakest posture)

When no OS keyring is available — the canonical case is **headless Linux with no
Secret Service** — the root key falls back to a file at `~/.writ/vault.key`.

- The file is created `0600`, opened with `O_NOFOLLOW`, and its owner + mode are
  checked on every open. On Windows the fallback is **DPAPI-wrapped**.
- **This is the weakest at-rest posture.** Anyone who can read your home
  directory (another local admin, a backup that captured `~/.writ`, malware
  running as your user) obtains the root key and therefore the **entire decrypted
  database**. The keyring-backed path does not have this exposure.
- The app **logs this fallback loudly** at startup so it is never silent.
- On servers / headless deployments, gate the root behind an env-injected
  `WRIT_VAULT_WRAP` secret rather than relying on the bare `vault.key` file. The
  headless `writ-agentd` never uses the interactive app-lock passphrase (it would
  block launchd/systemd auto-restart); it uses the keyring or `WRIT_VAULT_WRAP`.

If you require strong at-rest protection on a headless host, either provide a
Secret Service keyring or set `WRIT_VAULT_WRAP`; do not rely on the bare file
fallback.

---

## Data deletion / right-to-erasure stance

The desktop is a **single-user local store**: all your data is on your own
machine, so for local data **you are your own data controller**. Cloud-retained
metadata exists only when you link, and is governed by the Writ Cloud privacy
policy.

"Delete all my data" / per-asset hard-delete performs `secure_delete` + DB row
deletion + janitor-guarded file unlink, and "reset to factory" wipes `~/.writ`
(including the keyring entry). However — per the bounded claim above — **true
single-file crypto-erase is not guaranteed** under the shared file-master key.
Erasure is honest best-effort, not a cryptographic shred guarantee. We state this
plainly rather than over-claiming GDPR "right to erasure."

---

## How the security stack is verified (so claims are not just asserted)

- **Cipher-active fail-closed gate.** `local::db::assert_cipher_active` reads
  `PRAGMA cipher_version` at open and refuses to start if it is empty (which is
  what plain SQLite returns). This is **load-bearing**: if `sqlx` ever resolved a
  cipher-less `libsqlite3-sys`, `PRAGMA key` would silently no-op and `writ.db`
  would be written **plaintext while appearing to work**. The `sqlcipher-link-gate`
  CI job builds `--features local` and runs this test on every PR
  (SECURITY_AND_ENTITLEMENTS_SPEC.md §1.5, SUPPLY_CHAIN.md).
- **Supply-chain gates.** `cargo-deny` (advisories / licenses / bans / sources)
  + `cargo audit` run as required merge gates; an SBOM is generated per release.
  See `SUPPLY_CHAIN.md` and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- **Entitlement verification is reflection-only.** Desktop-held entitlements are
  Ed25519-JWS signed by the cloud and verified against a **pinned** public key,
  but they **never** gate enforcement or billing — every paid/metered capability
  is re-resolved server-side per call. See CLOUD_LINK_CONTRACT.md and
  SECURITY_AND_ENTITLEMENTS_SPEC.md Part 2.
- **Loopback hardening.** The local API binds `127.0.0.1` **by default**, behind a
  single `0600` bearer token + Origin/Host allowlist (DNS-rebinding defense). It
  rejects cloud tokens (`wto_`/`wtr_`/`wte`) — they are never local-API tokens. LAN
  exposure is an **explicit opt-in** with the same token + rebind guards still in
  force — see **Network exposure** below.

---

## Network exposure (loopback default, opt-in LAN)

The standalone daemon (`writ-agentd`) is **loopback-only by default**: it binds
`127.0.0.1` and is **never reachable from the network**. Nothing on your LAN — or
the wider internet — can reach the local API/MCP/OpenAI surface unless you take an
explicit action.

You may **opt in** to expose the API on your LAN (so other devices on the same
network can call it — e.g. an MCP client on another machine, a home-lab box) via a
UI button. This persists `network_exposed = true` under `[server]` in
`~/.writ/config.toml` (env override `WRIT_NETWORK_EXPOSE`) and, **on the next
daemon restart**, binds `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) instead of loopback. The bind is
fixed for a running listener's lifetime — toggling the flag never silently re-binds
a live process; the app applies it by restarting the sidecar.

The security posture when exposed:

- **The bearer token is ALWAYS required**, in both modes. Loopback and LAN callers
  alike must present a valid `wlt_` UI token or a scoped `wlk_` client key; there is
  no anonymous access in either mode.
- **DNS-rebind protection stays enforced.** The Origin/Host allowlist still rejects
  foreign browser origins (e.g. `http://evil.example`). When exposed it additionally
  accepts only the daemon's **own** bind/LAN address (loopback plus this machine's
  resolved LAN IP); a different LAN IP, a wrong port, or any foreign origin is still
  rejected. A browser page on another site cannot rebind to your daemon.
- **Defensive bind guard.** The daemon **refuses to bind any non-loopback address
  unless `network_exposed` is explicitly true**, so an accidental or forced
  non-loopback bind can never expose the API silently. Binding a non-loopback
  address emits a clear `WARNING` log line.

**Recommendations when you expose on the LAN:**

- Mint and hand out a **scoped `wlk_` key** (least-privilege: `read` or `run`,
  not the full-access `wlt_` UI token) for the calling device.
- Enable the **app-lock** so secret-touching routes stay sealed (HTTP `423`) until
  you authenticate, even from a LAN caller.
- Treat exposure as trusted-LAN-only. There is **no TLS** on the local listener —
  do not port-forward it to the public internet; tunnel over SSH/WireGuard/a
  reverse proxy with TLS if you need remote access.
- `GET /v1/network/status` reflects the **currently-running** bind
  (`exposed`/`bind_host`/`port`/`lan_url`); after toggling, `needs_restart` from
  `POST /v1/network/expose` signals the pending restart.

---

## Reconciliation

Any claim in the README, website, in-app copy, or release notes that exceeds the
**"What is explicitly NOT claimed"** list above is a defect. When in doubt, this
file wins. Cross-references: SECURITY_AND_ENTITLEMENTS_SPEC.md §1.6 / §2.1,
DESKTOP_APP_PLAN.md §0 / §9, PRODUCTION_READINESS.md PROD-21 / PROD-24,
CLOUD_LINK_CONTRACT.md, SUPPLY_CHAIN.md.

# Troubleshooting

Before anything else: **Settings → About** gives you the app version and a button to
open the log directory. Both are the first two things any bug report needs.

## "Engine stopped" in the bottom-left corner

The app is a thin window over a background engine (`writ-agentd`) that does the actual
browser work. The pill shows red when the window cannot reach it on `127.0.0.1`.

1. Click the **▶** next to the pill to restart the engine.
2. If it will not start, check the logs (**Settings → About → Open logs**) for the
   `writ-agentd` lines at the end.
3. A firewall or endpoint-security product that blocks **loopback** connections will
   break this. The engine listens only on `127.0.0.1` and never on a public interface —
   allow the app to talk to itself.
4. If a previous run left a stale process, quit Writ fully and relaunch.

## "Network error — check your connection"

This almost always means the same thing as the red pill: the window cannot reach the
local engine. It is not about your internet connection. Follow the steps above.

## Recording opens a blank browser, or will not start

Writ needs a Chromium runtime. **Settings → Engine & Data** shows which one it resolved
and where it lives.

- If it reports none, install it from that screen (about 150 MB).
- If a download failed part-way, install it again — a partial download is discarded
  rather than used.
- On Linux, the app needs a working WebKitGTK for its own window; a missing system
  library shows up as the app failing to launch at all rather than a blank browser.

## A recorded workflow used to work and now fails

Sites change. A step that pointed at a button that has moved or been renamed will fail
on replay. Open the workflow, find the failing step, and re-record just that step —
the rest of the workflow is preserved.

If the site added a login wall or 2FA, attach a **persona** so the run can sign in.

## Updates aren't installing

See [`AUTO_UPDATE.md`](./AUTO_UPDATE.md). The common causes, in order:

1. Updates are set to **Disabled** in Settings, or a machine policy disabled them.
2. The machine cannot reach the update host.
3. The update was fetched but **refused verification** — the app deliberately fails
   closed here and keeps running the version you have. If this persists, report it: a
   manifest that will not verify is worth looking at.

## The app will not open on macOS

If Gatekeeper reports that it cannot check the app for malicious software, the download
is likely incomplete. Re-download and verify the hash against `SHA256SUMS` rather than
bypassing the check. Releases are signed with an Apple Developer ID and notarized.

## Everything is broken and I want a clean slate

Quit the app, then move (do not delete, at first) your data directory:

```bash
mv ~/.writ ~/.writ.broken          # macOS / Linux
```

```powershell
Move-Item $env:USERPROFILE\.writ $env:USERPROFILE\.writ.broken   # Windows
```

Relaunch. You get a fresh install, and your old workflows and credentials are still in
the `.broken` directory if you need to recover something. **Deleting that directory
permanently destroys your workflows and stored credentials** — it is not recoverable
from anywhere else unless you had linked a cloud account.

## Filing a good bug report

[Open an issue](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-desktop/issues/new/choose) with:

- the app version (**Settings → About**) and your OS + version
- what you did, what you expected, what happened
- the relevant tail of the logs

**Please do not paste logs without reading them first** — they can contain URLs you
automate and page content. Redact anything you would not post publicly. If the problem
is a security vulnerability, do not open an issue at all: follow
[`SECURITY.md`](../SECURITY.md).

# Updates

Writ Desktop updates itself. This page describes what that means, what is verified
before anything is installed, and how to turn it off or point it somewhere else.

## What happens

1. The app asks the release channel whether a newer version exists.
2. If one is announced, the app fetches the release **manifest** — a small signed
   document describing the version, the artifacts, and their hashes.
3. The manifest's signature is checked against an Ed25519 public key **compiled into the
   application**. The key is not fetched, so a compromised update server cannot supply
   its own key. The signing algorithm is fixed in code; there is no negotiable algorithm
   field to downgrade.
4. Only if that check passes does the app download the installer, confirm its hash
   matches the manifest, and stage it.
5. The update applies on the next restart.

Anything that fails — an unknown signing key, a bad signature, a hash mismatch, an
expired manifest, or an attempt to move you to an *older* version — is refused, and the
app carries on running the version you already have. There is no path where an
unverified update is installed.

## Turning it off

**Settings → General → Updates.**

- **Automatic** (default) — check, verify, and stage updates in the background.
- **Disabled** — never check. You update by downloading a release yourself.

Disabling updates does not disable anything else. The app is fully functional offline.

## Managed deployments

If your organisation delivers a machine policy, it can:

- force **`update_mode`** to `disabled`, so the app never checks; or
- set **`update_mode`** to `managed` together with an **`update_feed_url`** pointing at
  an internal mirror you control, so machines fetch both the manifest and the artifacts
  from inside your network.

A machine policy is not user-overridable when present. Signature verification is
**not** relaxed for an internal feed: a mirrored manifest must still be signed by the
key compiled into the application, so mirroring is a distribution decision, not a trust
decision.

## Release channels

| Channel | Who it is for |
|---|---|
| `stable` | everyone, by default |
| `beta` | opt-in, pre-release builds |

Pre-release versions are marked as such on the releases page.

## Verifying an update by hand

If you would rather not let the app update itself, disable updates and install releases
manually. Every release carries `SHA256SUMS` computed over the signed artifacts — see
[`INSTALL.md`](./INSTALL.md#verifying-your-download).

## If an update fails

The app keeps running the version you have. Check **Settings → About** for the current
version, and the release notes in
[`CHANGELOG.md`](../CHANGELOG.md) for whether a known issue applies. If it keeps
failing, [open an issue](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-desktop/issues/new/choose) with
your version and OS — and see
[`TROUBLESHOOTING.md`](./TROUBLESHOOTING.md#updates-arent-installing).

name: Feature request
description: Suggest something Writ Desktop should be able to do.
labels: ["enhancement", "needs-triage"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        The most useful requests describe the **problem** rather than the solution — it
        often turns out there is already a way to do it, or a better shape for it.

  - type: textarea
    id: problem
    attributes:
      label: What are you trying to do?
      description: The task or workflow you are stuck on, not the feature you imagine.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: today
    attributes:
      label: How do you handle it today?
      description: Manually, with another tool, with a workaround inside Writ, or not at all.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: idea
    attributes:
      label: What would you like Writ to do?
      description: Optional — if you already have a shape in mind, describe it here.

  - type: dropdown
    id: area
    attributes:
      label: Which part of the app?
      options:
        - Recording workflows
        - Running / scheduling
        - Monitors
        - Automations
        - Crawling
        - MCP / API surfaces
        - Personas & secrets
        - Settings / app shell
        - Not sure
    validations:
      required: true

name: Bug report
description: Something in Writ Desktop is broken or behaves unexpectedly.
labels: ["bug", "needs-triage"]
body:
  - type: markdown
    attributes:
      value: |
        Thanks for reporting. Two things first:

        - **Security vulnerability?** Do not file it here. Follow
          [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/usewrit/writ-desktop/blob/main/SECURITY.md)
          so it can be fixed before it is public.
        - **Logs can contain the URLs you automate and page content.** Read anything you
          paste and redact what you would not post publicly.

  - type: input
    id: version
    attributes:
      label: Writ Desktop version
      description: Settings → About
      placeholder: "1.0.0"
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: dropdown
    id: os
    attributes:
      label: Operating system
      options:
        - macOS (Apple silicon)
        - macOS (Intel)
        - Windows
        - Linux (deb)
        - Linux (AppImage)
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: input
    id: os_version
    attributes:
      label: OS version
      placeholder: "macOS 15.1 / Windows 11 23H2 / Ubuntu 24.04"
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: what_happened
    attributes:
      label: What happened
      description: What you did, what you expected, and what you got instead.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: steps
    attributes:
      label: Steps to reproduce
      placeholder: |
        1.
        2.
        3.
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: dropdown
    id: reproducible
    attributes:
      label: Does it happen every time?
      options:
        - Every time
        - Sometimes
        - Happened once
    validations:
      required: true

  - type: textarea
    id: logs
    attributes:
      label: Relevant logs
      description: >
        Settings → About → Open logs. Paste the tail around the failure — not the whole
        file. Redact URLs, page content, and anything else you would not post publicly.
      render: shell

  - type: textarea
    id: extra
    attributes:
      label: Anything else
      description: Screenshots, workarounds you found, whether it started after an update.
